statements.impact_statement: GO-2026-5932: the golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp packages (openpgp, armor, clearsign, elgamal, errors, packet and s2k) are unmaintained, unsafe by design and have known security issues; the Go vulnerability database marks every golang.org/x/crypto release before the commit that moves them into a separate module as affected, with no individual functions listed: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5932, https://go.dev/issue/44226, https://go.dev/issue/81227, https://github.com/golang/crypto/commit/2f1f834330b2d36ab3db8bfb33aaa1ac16794588 . We downloaded every docker-cli-buildx apk that the Alpine 3.23 index of the DHI Alpine repository lists, 29 versions from 0.33.0-r1 to 0.39.1-r1 for x86_64 and aarch64 (0.34.1-r0 is published for aarch64 only), 57 apks, and checked each download against its index checksum; no docker-cli-buildx package is published in the DHI Alpine security repository. Each apk holds one regular file and no symbolic links: /usr/libexec/docker/cli-plugins/docker-buildx, a Go program. We read its Go build information and its function table from the Go line table, which finds runtime.main in every build. The golang.org/x/crypto version in the build information, the same on both architectures, is: 0.33.0-r1 to 0.33.0-r2 with 0.48.0; 0.34.1-r0 to 0.34.1-r2 with 0.50.0; 0.35.0-r0 to 0.35.0-r3 with 0.52.0; 0.36.0-r0 to 0.36.1-r3 with 0.54.0; 0.36.1-r4 with 0.55.0; 0.37.0-r0 to 0.37.2-r1 with 0.56.0; 0.37.2-r2 to 0.38.1-r0 with 0.57.0; 0.38.1-r1 to 0.39.1-r0 with 0.58.0; 0.39.1-r1 with 0.59.0. Every build before 0.39.1-r1 uses a release inside the affected range; 0.39.1-r1 uses 0.59.0, which contains the fix commit. In every build the function table contains golang.org/x/crypto functions from no packages other than argon2, bcrypt, blake2b, blowfish, cast5, chacha20, cryptobyte, curve25519, hkdf, internal/poly1305, nacl/sign, pbkdf2, scrypt, ssh and ssh/agent, and no function whose name starts with golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp, a prefix match that also covers closures and method-value wrappers. A byte search of every build's program for golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp followed by a dot or a slash finds nothing, while the same search for golang.org/x/crypto/ finds matches in every build. The program does link the OpenPGP packages of github.com/ProtonMail/go-crypto, the maintained fork the advisory recommends, which is a different module and not covered by this advisory. As a check, a test program that calls openpgp.ReadArmoredKeyRing and armor.Decode, built with golang.org/x/crypto 0.58.0, Go 1.26.11, CGO_ENABLED=0 and -trimpath for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64, shows 86 golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp functions with the same function-table reader and 263 matches with the same byte search. The golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp packages are not compiled into any build of this package.
